welcome.label: Welcome · postcards from Maine

parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: Postcards from Maine
parts.body: Why is Dr. Reyes’s pond busy in January when Bea’s pond in Maine is quiet? Does Florida have seasons?

welcome.script:
(Hold up a postcard.) Welcome back, scientists! Remember Dr. Reyes’s pond? It’s January now.

[ON SCREEN: Dr. Reyes’s pond]
Her pond is busier than ever. Ducks! Robins! Even a manatee.

[ON SCREEN: Postcard 1]
But her friend Bea in Maine sent this. Her pond is frozen solid.

[ON SCREEN: Postcard 2]
And the bears? Asleep under the snow.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
Bea thinks Florida doesn’t have seasons. Is she right? Find four clues. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · two winters (Clue 1)

parts.label: 👆 How to play
parts.title: Two winters
rows: Drag it to Florida or Maine, or tap it, then tap the place.

warmup.script:
(Shiver and rub your arms.) Brrr! Close your eyes and picture January. What do you see outside?

[ON SCREEN: Manatees]
Here’s one January in Florida.

[ON SCREEN: Bear]
And here’s one in Maine. Same month! Hmm, how can that be?

[ON SCREEN: How to play]
Sort each photo into Florida or Maine. Then list three ways the two Januarys are different. Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s hint.

part1.label: Part 1 · turn the calendar (Clue 2)

parts.label: 📅 The calendar
parts.title: Turn the calendar
rows: Tap a page: January, April, July, October.

part1.script:
(Flip an imaginary calendar page.) Let’s travel through a whole year in one minute!

[ON SCREEN: Robin]
This robin might eat berries in Florida in January, and pull up worms in Maine in July. Where is it in between?

[ON SCREEN: The calendar]
Tap each calendar page. Read across each row to see what happens in Florida and in Maine. Who stays? Who leaves? Who sleeps? Press Listen.

part3.label: Part 3 · the manatee water test (Clue 3)
part3.script:
(Dip a finger in a cup of water and shiver.) Some animals feel cold water more than we do.

[ON SCREEN: The river]
Manatees eat seagrass in Florida’s rivers.

[ON SCREEN: The spring]
But this spring stays about 72 degrees all year. Hmm. Why would they crowd in here?

[ON SCREEN: The test]
Scientists change only one thing at a time. Change the river temperature, run the morning, and watch. Try cold and warm. Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 4 · build the seasonal model (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🧩 Three steps
parts.title: Build the seasonal model
rows: Fill both circles: a plant, an animal, the weather.
Tap a plant, then the animal that eats it.

explore.script:
(Draw two circles in the air.) Scientists use models to show how things connect.

[ON SCREEN: Ducks]
These ducks nest up north. So why are they in Florida in January? A model can show us.

[ON SCREEN: Three steps]
Fill a Florida circle and a Maine circle. Add the food-energy arrows. Then point the migration arrow the right way. That’s your last clue. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Postcards from Maine
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Four places to write
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case at the top of this tab: why is Dr. Reyes’s pond so busy in January?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, your own two-region model in Part C, and a CER. Want to sketch your model? That’s a bonus. Stuck? Press Hint under any box. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Florida doesn’t really have seasons. It’s just summer all year.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says Florida doesn’t really have seasons. It’s just summer all year. Sounds like Bea! Do you agree?

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Remember CER. Tap your side and two facts from today. Think about the manatees and the ducks. Then explain how your facts prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 📮 Your specimen
parts.title: Postcard from Maine
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Resources
parts.body: The water, sunlight and wind people use, and which ones can run out.

closing.script:
Case closed! Florida does have seasons, just milder ones. That’s why the ducks and robins come here for the winter.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and Bea’s postcard goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time: the resources we all use, like water, sunlight and wind. Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
